payload.name: Verify duplicate before skipping memory candidate
payload.description: When a Construction Agent is about to SKIP an extracted candidate because it appears duplicate, verify an equivalent memory actually exists in the retrieved related-memory pool before skipping. If no such memory is present, do not SKIP.
content: Before choosing SKIP for a candidate on duplicate grounds, confirm that an equivalent memory is actually present in the retrieved related-memory pool or current snapshot version.
If no existing memory supports the claimed duplication, do not skip: ADD the candidate, or MERGE only when a concrete target memory exists.
A generic 'duplicate information already represented' reason is not sufficient when the related-memory pool is empty or contains no matching memory.

solves: During batched memory construction, a candidate can be marked as duplicate and skipped even when the related-memory pool contains no equivalent memory, so the fact is never persisted. This rule ensures duplicate checks compare against actually retrieved existing memories rather than inferred or generic duplication. It applies to future construction decisions where SKIP is considered for a new candidate and no matching memory is visible in the retrieved pool.
